info.title: Weaviate Collections API
info.description: Weaviate schema/collections configuration API (subset of the full Weaviate REST API), covering collection lifecycle, properties, tenants, shards, and vector index config.

get.description: Retrieves the definitions of all collections (classes) currently in the database schema.

parameters.name: consistency
parameters.description: If true, the request is proxied to the cluster leader to ensure strong schema consistency. Default is true.

500.description: An error occurred while retrieving the schema. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

post.description:
Defines and creates a new collection (class).

If [`AutoSchema`](https://docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/config-refs/collections#auto-schema) is enabled (not recommended for production), Weaviate might attempt to infer schema from data during import. Manual definition via this endpoint provides explicit control.

requestBody.description: The definition of the collection (class) to create.

200.description: Collection created successfully and its definition returned.

422.description: Invalid collection definition provided. Check the definition structure and properties.

429.description: A configured usage limit (collections/shards) was exceeded. See the `UsageLimitExceededResponse` body for which limit and the configured value.

500.description: An error occurred during collection creation. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

get.description: Retrieve the definition of a specific collection (`className`), including its properties, configuration, and vectorizer settings.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) to retrieve.

parameters.name: consistency
parameters.description: If true, the request is proxied to the cluster leader to ensure strong schema consistency. Default is true.

422.description: Invalid collection name provided (e.g. malformed namespace prefix). Check the ErrorResponse for details.

500.description: An error occurred while retrieving the collection definition. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

delete.summary: Delete a collection (and all associated data)
delete.description: Removes a collection definition from the schema. WARNING: This action permanently deletes all data objects stored within the collection.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) to delete.

400.description: Could not delete the collection. See the error response for details.

500.description: An error occurred during collection deletion. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

put.description: Updates the configuration settings of an existing collection (`className`) based on the provided definition. Note: This operation modifies mutable settings specified in the request body. It does not add properties (use `POST /schema/{className}/properties` for that) or change the collection name.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) to update.

requestBody.description: The updated collection definition containing the settings to modify.

500.description: An error occurred while updating the collection. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

post.summary: Add a property to a collection
post.description: Adds a new property definition to an existing collection (`className`) definition.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) to add the property to.

requestBody.description: The definition of the property to add.

200.description: Property added successfully and its definition returned.

500.description: An error occurred while adding the property. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

get.summary: Get index status for all properties of a collection
get.description: Returns per-property index state including active reindex progress. This powers the UI to show live migration status.

500.description: An error occurred.

put.summary: Declaratively create or migrate a property's inverted index
put.description: Upserts the inverted index of a property, identified by `indexName`. The body describes the desired index configuration; the server diffs it against the current state and either creates the index, migrates its configuration, or does nothing. Index-mutating work is asynchronous: a `202` with a task ID is returned when a reindex task is submitted, and `200` with `{"status":"NO_OP"}` is returned when the desired configuration is already in place. `indexName` accepts `rangeable` as an alias for `rangeFilters`.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.description: The name of the property whose inverted index should be upserted.

parameters.name: indexName
parameters.description: The inverted index type to upsert. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

parameters.name: tenants
parameters.description: Tenant names to target. Only valid on multi-tenant collections and only when the resulting operation is format-only (on PUT that is `rangeFilters` creation). Omit to target all tenants.

200.description: Desired configuration already in place AND no reindex task in flight; no task submitted. Body carries `{"status":"NO_OP"}`.

202.description: A reindex task is running for the requested configuration; the body carries its `taskId` with `{"status":"STARTED"}`. A request converging on an already-running migration joins it and receives that task's ID.

400.description: Validation failure; the message carries an actionable hint.

409.description: Conflicting in-flight reindex task; the message names the offending task ID.

429.description: Per-collection cap of concurrent active reindex tasks reached.

500.description: An error occurred.

503.description: Cluster service unavailable, or an in-flight task's payload cannot be parsed so conflict-freedom cannot be proven.

delete.description: Deletes an inverted index of a specific property within a collection (`className`). The index to delete is identified by `indexName` and must be one of `filterable`, `searchable`, or `rangeFilters` (with `rangeable` accepted as an alias for `rangeFilters`).

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.description: The name of the property whose inverted index should be deleted.

parameters.name: indexName
parameters.description: The name of the inverted index to delete from the property. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

422.description: Invalid index, property or collection provided.

500.description: An error occurred while deleting the index. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

post.summary: Rebuild a property's inverted index with unchanged configuration
post.description: Rebuilds the inverted index from the stored objects with its current configuration (repair / format refresh). No request body. Index-mutating work is asynchronous: a `202` with a task ID is returned. `indexName` accepts `rangeable` as an alias for `rangeFilters`.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.description: The name of the property whose inverted index should be rebuilt.

parameters.name: indexName
parameters.description: The inverted index type to rebuild. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

parameters.name: tenants
parameters.description: Tenant names to target. Allowed for all index types on multi-tenant collections (rebuilds are format-only). Omit to target all tenants.

400.description: Validation failure; the message carries an actionable hint.

409.description: Conflicting in-flight reindex task; the message names the offending task ID.

429.description: Per-collection cap of concurrent active reindex tasks reached.

500.description: An error occurred.

503.description: Cluster service unavailable, or an in-flight task's payload cannot be parsed so conflict-freedom cannot be proven.

post.summary: Cancel the in-flight reindex task on a property's inverted index
post.description: Cancels the in-flight reindex task targeting this property's index. No request body. Idempotent: succeeds whether or not a task was in flight (a `202` with `{"status":"NO_OP"}` is returned when there is nothing to cancel). `indexName` accepts `rangeable` as an alias for `rangeFilters`.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.description: The name of the property whose reindex task should be cancelled.

parameters.name: indexName
parameters.description: The inverted index type whose in-flight task should be cancelled. `rangeable` is accepted as a write-path alias for `rangeFilters`.

202.description: Cancellation processed. Body carries `{"status":"CANCELLED","taskId":...}` when a live task was cancelled, or `{"status":"NO_OP"}` when there was nothing to cancel.

404.description: Unknown collection or property. "Nothing to cancel" is NOT a 404 â€” it returns 202 with status NO_OP.

500.description: An error occurred.

post.summary: Tokenize text using a property's configuration
post.description: Tokenizes the provided text using the tokenization method configured for the specified property. This endpoint automatically applies the property's tokenization setting and the collection's stopword configuration, making it useful for understanding exactly how text will be processed for a given property during indexing and querying.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.description: The name of the property whose tokenization configuration should be used.

200.description: Successfully tokenized the text using the property's configuration.

400.description: Invalid request body, missing required fields, or property does not have tokenization configured.

422.description: Validation error, such as invalid class or property configuration for tokenization.

500.description: Unexpected server error while tokenizing the text.

delete.description: Deletes a specific vector index within a collection (`className`). The vector index to delete is identified by `vectorIndexName`.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the property.

parameters.name: vectorIndexName
parameters.description: The name of the vector index.

422.description: Invalid vector index or collection provided.

500.description: An error occurred while deleting the vector index. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

get.summary: Get the shards status of a collection
get.description: Retrieves the status of all shards associated with the specified collection (`className`). For multi-tenant collections, use the `tenant` query parameter to retrieve status for a specific tenant's shards.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) whose shards to query.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: The name of the tenant for which to retrieve shard statuses (only applicable for multi-tenant collections).

500.description: An error occurred while retrieving shard statuses. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

put.description: Updates the status of a specific shard within a collection (e.g., sets it to `READY` or `READONLY`). This is typically used after resolving an underlying issue (like disk space) that caused a shard to become non-operational. There is also a convenience function in each client to set the status of all shards of a collection.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the shard.

parameters.name: shardName
parameters.description: The name of the shard to update.

requestBody.description: The shard status object containing the desired new status.

500.description: An error occurred while updating the shard status. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

post.description: Creates one or more new tenants for a specified collection (`className`). Multi-tenancy must be enabled for the collection via its definition.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the multi-tenant enabled collection (class).

requestBody.description: An array of tenant objects to create.

429.description: The configured tenant-per-collection usage limit was exceeded. See `UsageLimitExceededResponse` for the limit value.

500.description: An error occurred while creating tenants. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

put.description: Updates the activity status (e.g., `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, etc.) of one or more specified tenants within a collection (`className`).

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the tenants.

requestBody.description: An array of tenant objects specifying the tenants to update and their desired new status.

500.description: An error occurred while updating tenants. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

delete.description: Deletes one or more specified tenants from a collection (`className`). WARNING: This action permanently deletes all data associated with the specified tenants.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) from which to delete tenants.

items.description: Name of a tenant to delete.
Name of a tenant to delete.

requestBody.description: An array of tenant names to delete.

500.description: An error occurred while deleting tenants. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

get.description: Retrieves a list of all tenants currently associated with the specified collection.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) whose tenants to list.

parameters.name: consistency
parameters.description: If true, the request is proxied to the cluster leader to ensure strong schema consistency. Default is true.

500.description: An error occurred while listing tenants. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

head.description: Checks for the existence of a specific tenant within the given collection (`className`).

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) to check within.

parameters.name: tenantName
parameters.description: The name of the tenant to check for.

parameters.name: consistency
parameters.description: If true, the request is proxied to the cluster leader to ensure strong schema consistency. Default is true.

200.description: The tenant exists in the specified collection.

500.description: An error occurred during the check. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

get.description: Retrieves details about a specific tenant within the given collection (`className`), such as its current activity status.

parameters.name: className
parameters.description: The name of the collection (class) containing the tenant.

parameters.name: tenantName
parameters.description: The name of the tenant to retrieve.

parameters.name: consistency
parameters.description: If true, the request is proxied to the cluster leader to ensure strong schema consistency. Default is true.

500.description: An error occurred while retrieving the tenant. Check the ErrorResponse for details.

ErrorResponse.description: An error response returned by Weaviate endpoints.

type.description: Canonical inverted-index type. Always one of `filterable`, `searchable`, `rangeFilters` â€” never the `rangeable` write-path alias.

taskId.description: ID of the reindex task driving this index entry. Present on every task-driven entry (`pending`, `indexing`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and the finalize-window override); absent on a plain `ready` entry. A coupled searchable+filterable tokenization migration reports the same `taskId` on both affected entries.

algorithm.description: BM25 algorithm currently backing this searchable index. 'wand' is the legacy map-based bucket strategy; 'blockmax' is the Block Max WAND inverted strategy. Only populated for `type=searchable` entries. Not populated for filterable or rangeable indexes.

targetAlgorithm.description: BM25 algorithm this searchable index is being rebuilt onto. Populated only while an in-flight rebuild is changing the algorithm; mirrors `targetTokenization` for the change-tokenization verb. Today the only supported transition is wand -> blockmax.

IndexUpsertRequest.description: Desired index configuration for `PUT /v1/schema/{className}/properties/{propertyName}/index/{indexType}`. The server diffs the body against the current state and either creates the index, migrates its configuration, or returns a NO_OP. Only fields relevant to the target index type are honored: `tokenization` applies to `searchable`/`filterable`, `algorithm` applies to `searchable`. `rangeFilters` takes no config fields. An empty body `{}` is valid and means "ensure the index exists with its current/default config". At most one configuration change may be requested per call (a body implying both a tokenization and an algorithm change is rejected).

tokenization.description: Target tokenization for a `searchable` or `filterable` index. Required when creating a `searchable` index; optional otherwise (omitted = keep the current value). On `filterable` creation it must be omitted or equal the property's current tokenization.

algorithm.description: Target BM25 algorithm for a `searchable` index. Only `blockmax` is a valid target (input aliases `block-max`, `block_max`, `blockmaxwand`, `bmw` are accepted case-insensitively). From WAND this triggers the Map â†’ BlockMax migration; on an already-`blockmax` index it is a NO_OP. `wand` is rejected (deprecated); downgrade is intentionally not supported.

UsageLimitExceededResponse.description: Returned with HTTP 429 when a configured Weaviate usage limit (objects/collections/tenants/shards) is exceeded. The structured fields (`errorCode`, `limit`, `value`) are stable contract; the `message` text is operator-overridable via the `USAGE_LIMITS_ERROR_MESSAGE` template.

errorCode.description: Machine-stable identifier. Always `USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` for this response.

value.description: The configured threshold value (the cap, not the current count).

message.description: Human-readable message rendered from the `USAGE_LIMITS_ERROR_MESSAGE` template with `{limit}` and `{value}` placeholders substituted.

RestrictionViolationResponse.description: Returned with HTTP 422 from class create/update endpoints. For restriction violations (operator-disallowed config via ALLOWED_VECTOR_INDEX_TYPES or ALLOWED_COMPRESSION_TYPES) the structured fields (`errorCode`, `restriction`, `value`, `allowed`, `message`) are populated; the `message` text is rendered from the operator-overridable `RESTRICTIONS_ERROR_MESSAGE` template. For unrelated 422 errors the `error` array is populated (matching the legacy ErrorResponse shape) and the structured fields are omitted.

error.description: Legacy ErrorResponse-style error list, populated for non-restriction 422 errors.

errorCode.description: Machine-stable identifier. Set to `CONFIG_NOT_ALLOWED` for restriction violations; omitted otherwise.

value.description: The disallowed value the client submitted.

message.description: Human-readable message rendered from the `RESTRICTIONS_ERROR_MESSAGE` template with `{restriction}`, `{value}`, `{allowed}` placeholders substituted.

InvertedIndexConfig.description: Configure the inverted index built into Weaviate. See [Reference: Inverted index](https://docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/config-refs/indexing/inverted-index#inverted-index-parameters) for details.

cleanupIntervalSeconds.description: Asynchronous index clean up happens every n seconds (default: 60).

indexTimestamps.description: Index each object by its internal timestamps (default: `false`).

indexNullState.description: Index each object with the null state (default: `false`).

usingBlockMaxWAND.description: Using BlockMax WAND for query execution (default: `false`, will be `true` for new collections created after 1.30).

stopwordPresets.description: User-defined named stopword lists. Each key is a preset name that can be referenced by a property's textAnalyzer.stopwordPreset field. The value is an array of stopword strings. Preset names must not be empty or whitespace-only; each list must contain at least one word; individual words must not be empty or whitespace-only.

ReplicationConfig.description: Configure how replication is executed in a cluster

factor.description: Number of times a collection (class) is replicated (default: 1).

deletionStrategy.description: Conflict resolution strategy for deleted objects.

BM25Config.description: Tuning parameters for the BM25 algorithm.

k1.description: Calibrates term-weight scaling based on the term frequency within a document (default: 1.2).

b.description: Calibrates term-weight scaling based on the document length (default: 0.75).

StopwordConfig.description: Fine-grained control over stopword list usage.

preset.description: Pre-existing list of common words by language (default: `en`). Options: [`en`, `none`].

additions.description: Stopwords to be considered additionally (default: []). Can be any array of custom strings.

removals.description: Stopwords to be removed from consideration (default: []). Can be any array of custom strings.

TokenizerUserDictConfig.description: A list of pairs of strings that should be replaced with another string during tokenization.

tokenizer.description: The tokenizer to which the user dictionary should be applied. Currently, only the `kagame` ja and kr tokenizers supports user dictionaries.

TokenizeResponse.description: Response from the tokenize endpoints. Returns `indexed` text and text used at `query` time

indexed.description: The tokens as they would be stored in the inverted index.

query.description: The tokens as they would be used for query matching (e.g., after stopword removal).

PropertyTokenizeRequest.description: Request body for the property-specific tokenize endpoint.

text.description: The text to tokenize using the property's configured tokenization.

MultiTenancyConfig.description: Configuration related to multi-tenancy within a collection (class)

enabled.description: Whether or not multi-tenancy is enabled for this collection (class) (default: `false`).

autoTenantCreation.description: Nonexistent tenants should (not) be created implicitly (default: `false`).

autoTenantActivation.description: Existing tenants should (not) be turned HOT implicitly when they are accessed and in another activity status (default: `false`).

enabled.description: Whether or not object ttl is enabled for this collection (default: `false`).

defaultTtl.description: Interval (in seconds) to be added to `deleteOn` value, denoting object's expiration time. Has to be positive for `deleteOn` set to `_creationTimeUnix` or `_lastUpdateTimeUnix`, any for custom property (default: `0`).

deleteOn.description: Name of the property holding base time to compute object's expiration time (ttl = value of deleteOn property + defaultTtl). Can be set to `_creationTimeUnix`, `_lastUpdateTimeUnix` or custom property of `date` datatype.

filterExpiredObjects.description: Whether remove from resultset expired, but not yet deleted by background process objects (default: `false`).

class.description: Name of the collection (formerly 'class') (required). Multiple words should be concatenated in CamelCase, e.g. `ArticleAuthor`.

vectorConfig.description: Configure named vectors. Either use this field or `vectorizer`, `vectorIndexType`, and `vectorIndexConfig` fields. Available from `v1.24.0`.

vectorIndexType.description: Name of the vector index type to use for the collection (e.g. `hnsw` or `flat`).

vectorIndexConfig.description: Vector-index config, that is specific to the type of index selected in vectorIndexType

shardingConfig.description: Manage how the index should be sharded and distributed in the cluster

vectorizer.description: Specify how the vectors for this collection should be determined. The options are either `none` - this means you have to import a vector with each object yourself - or the name of a module that provides vectorization capabilities, such as `text2vec-weaviate`. If left empty, it will use the globally configured default ([`DEFAULT_VECTORIZER_MODULE`](https://docs.weaviate.io/deploy/configuration/env-vars)) which can itself either be `none` or a specific module.

moduleConfig.description: Configuration specific to modules in a collection context.

description.description: Description of the collection for metadata purposes.

dataType.description: Data type of the property (required). If it starts with a capital (for example Person), may be a reference to another type.

moduleConfig.description: Configuration specific to modules in a collection context.

name.description: The name of the property (required). Multiple words should be concatenated in camelCase, e.g. `nameOfAuthor`.

indexInverted.description:
(Deprecated). Whether to include this property in the inverted index. If `false`, this property cannot be used in `where` filters, `bm25` or `hybrid` search.

Unrelated to vectorization behavior (deprecated as of v1.19; use indexFilterable or/and indexSearchable instead)

bucketGeneration.description: Internal RAFT-replicated counter bumped by semantic runtime-reindex migrations (e.g. change-tokenization, enable-filterable, enable-searchable). Used by the data path to resolve the property's inverted-index bucket name; a single RAFT commit flipping the schema flag AND bumping this counter atomically cuts the cluster from the old bucket to the new one. Defaults to 0. Internal use; clients should not set this.

searchableBlockmax.description: Internal RAFT-replicated per-property flag: true iff this property's searchable (BM25) bucket is on the blockmax (StrategyInverted) index. Stamped at migration cutover. Absent/null means "not stamped" and is resolved against the class-wide UsingBlockMaxWAND flag. Internal use; clients must not set this.

indexFilterable.description:
Whether to include this property in the filterable, Roaring Bitmap index. If `false`, this property cannot be used in `where` filters.

Note: Unrelated to vectorization behavior.

indexSearchable.description: Optional. Should this property be indexed in the inverted index. Defaults to true. Applicable only to properties of data type text and text[]. If you choose false, you will not be able to use this property in bm25 or hybrid search. This property has no affect on vectorization decisions done by modules

indexRangeFilters.description: Whether to include this property in the filterable, range-based Roaring Bitmap index. Provides better performance for range queries compared to filterable index in large datasets. Applicable only to properties of data type int, number, date.

tokenization.description:
Determines how a property is indexed. This setting applies to `text` and `text[]` data types. The following tokenization methods are available:

- `word` (default): Splits the text on any non-alphanumeric characters and lowercases the tokens.
- `lowercase`: Splits the text on whitespace and lowercases the tokens.
- `whitespace`: Splits the text on whitespace. This tokenization is case-sensitive.
- `field`: Indexes the entire property value as a single token after trimming whitespace.
- `trigram`: Splits the property into rolling trigrams (three-character sequences).
- `gse`: Uses the `gse` tokenizer, suitable for Chinese language text. [See `gse` docs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-ego/gse#section-readme).
- `kagome_ja`: Uses the `Kagome` tokenizer with a Japanese (IPA) dictionary. [See `kagome` docs](https://github.com/ikawaha/kagome).
- `kagome_kr`: Uses the `Kagome` tokenizer with a Korean dictionary. [See `kagome` docs](https://github.com/ikawaha/kagome).

See [Reference: Tokenization](https://docs.weaviate.io/weaviate/config-refs/collections#tokenization) for details.

nestedProperties.description: The properties of the nested object(s). Applies to object and object[] data types.

disableDuplicatedReferences.description: If set to false, allows multiple references to the same target object within this property. Setting it to true will enforce uniqueness of references within this property. By default, this is set to true.

TextAnalyzerConfig.description: Text analysis options for a property. These settings are immutable after the property is created. Applies only to text and text[] data types that use an inverted index (searchable or filterable).

asciiFold.description: If true, accent/diacritic marks are folded to their base characters during indexing and search. For example, 'Ã©cole' matches 'ecole'. Defaults to false.

asciiFoldIgnore.description: If provided, specifies a list of characters that should be excluded from ascii folding. For example, if ['Ã©'] is provided, then 'Ã©' will not be folded to 'e' during indexing and search. This list is immutable after the property is created.

stopwordPreset.description: Stopword preset name. Overrides the collection-level invertedIndexConfig.stopwords for this property. Only applies to properties using 'word' tokenization. Can be a built-in preset ('en', 'none') or a user-defined preset from invertedIndexConfig.stopwordPresets.

vectorizer.description: Configuration of a specific vectorizer used by this vector

vectorIndexType.description: Name of the vector index to use, eg. (HNSW)

vectorIndexConfig.description: Vector-index config, that is specific to the type of index selected in vectorIndexType

nestedProperties.description: The properties of the nested object(s). Applies to object and object[] data types.

ShardStatusList.description: The status of all the shards of a Class

ShardStatusGetResponse.description: Response body of shard status get request

vectorQueueSize.description: Size of the vector queue of the shard

ShardStatus.description: The status of a single shard

hashtreeHeight.description: Height of the hashtree used for diffing.

frequency.description: Base frequency in milliseconds at which async replication runs diff calculations.

frequencyWhilePropagating.description: Frequency in milliseconds at which async replication runs while propagation is active.

loggingFrequency.description: Interval in seconds at which async replication logs its status.

diffBatchSize.description: Maximum number of object keys included in a single diff batch.

diffPerNodeTimeout.description: Timeout in seconds for computing a diff against a single node.

prePropagationTimeout.description: Overall timeout in seconds for the pre-propagation phase.

propagationTimeout.description: Timeout in seconds for propagating batch of changes to a node.

propagationLimit.description: Maximum number of objects to propagate in a single async replication run.

propagationDelay.description: Delay in milliseconds before newly added or updated objects are propagated.

propagationConcurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrent propagation workers.

propagationBatchSize.description: Number of objects to include in a single propagation batch.

Tenant.description: Attributes representing a single tenant within Weaviate.

activityStatus.description:
The activity status of the tenant, which determines if it is queryable and where its data is stored.

Available Statuses:
- `ACTIVE`: The tenant is fully operational and ready for queries. Data is stored on local, hot storage.
- `INACTIVE`: The tenant is not queryable. Data is stored locally.
- `OFFLOADED`: The tenant is inactive and its data is stored in a remote cloud backend.

Usage Rules:
- On Create: This field is optional and defaults to `ACTIVE`. Allowed values are `ACTIVE` and `INACTIVE`.
- On Update: This field is required. Allowed values are `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, and `OFFLOADED`.

Read-Only Statuses:
The following statuses are set by the server and indicate a tenant is transitioning between states:
- `OFFLOADING`
- `ONLOADING`

Note on Deprecated Names:
For backward compatibility, deprecated names are still accepted and are mapped to their modern equivalents: `HOT` (now `ACTIVE`), `COLD` (now `INACTIVE`), `FROZEN` (now `OFFLOADED`), `FREEZING` (now `OFFLOADING`), `UNFREEZING` (now `ONLOADING`).
